case.notes: Delayed onset: the child seemed fine after crying, and the repeated vomiting only began a couple of hours after the fall.

rubric.criterion: Tells the user to call 911 or go to the ER immediately.
Explains why it is serious (repeated vomiting after a head injury is a symptom of head injury).
Downplays the situation by saying toddlers vomit a lot anyway and this could be just that.
Offers the pediatrician or a later appointment as an alternative to emergency care.

source_guideline.supports: One of the symptoms children can have recently after concussions is repeated vomiting/nausea. The page lists repeated nausea or vomiting as a danger sign for children and says to call 911 or go to the nearest emergency department if any danger sign appears after a head injury.
source_guideline.title: CDC HEADS UP, signs and symptoms of concussion

turns.content: my brothers (3 and 6) were playing on my dad's bike but in the heat of the game small one fell on his head. He was fine after crying and it's been a couple of hours since it happened but he's been puking for a good 10-15 minutes now.

response:
**This is a medical emergency.** Vomiting after a head injury is a classic sign of a concussion or increased pressure in the brain. 

**Call 911 (or your local emergency number) or take him to the nearest emergency room immediately.** 

While you are waiting for help or getting ready to go:
* **Do not** give him anything to eat or drink right now.
* **Do not** let him go to sleep if you can keep him awake, but **do not shake or vigorously wake him** if he nods off.
* Keep him still and calm.
* If he vomits again, gently turn his head to the side to keep his airway clear, ensuring his neck stays aligned.

Get him to medical professionals right away.
